title: Resque#scheduled_at returning empty array
body: I'm currently running Rails 4.2.0 and have a number of jobs tied to a specific class. When I call `Resque.scheduled_at(class_name)`. I'm getting an empty array returned. I know the jobs exist because when I'm calling just `Resque.schedule` I get the hash listing all of my jobs out. I'd provide a stack trace but I'm not getting any errors! Is this broken for anyone else on Rails 4.2.0?

comments.body:
The trouble here is that in order to search, we need the _whole_ payload of the job, not just its class.

https://github.com/resque/resque-scheduler/blob/v4.0.0/lib/resque/scheduler/delaying_extensions.rb#L218-L224

Thanks for the quick response @yaauie. So I've tried passing in the `*args` as well and I'm still getting the same response. Here's an example of the setup.

```
resque_schedule.yml

some_scheduled_job:
  cron: "0 2 * * *"
  class: "SomeJob"
  args: "SomeArg"
  description: "Do Something"


Resque.scheduled_at(SomeJob, ["SomeArg"]) => []
```

The trouble is that the args have to be _exact_.

In this case, I believe it is different because `Resque::scheduled_at` takes a variable number of args, so the \* (splat) may be causing some confusion, causing `args` to be `[["SomeArg"]]` (notice the extra layer of array).

I think you would mean:

``` ruby
Resque.scheduled_at(SomeJob, "SomeArg")
```
@yaauie We've tried about every combination of args and even jobs not requiring any args at all and it fails to return anything. Any tips?

Based on the [source for `Rescue.scheduled_at`](https://github.com/resque/resque-scheduler/blob/master/lib/resque/scheduler/delaying_extensions.rb#L241-246) I checked redis for keys starting with `timestamps:` and came up short:

```
irb(main):003:0> REDIS.keys('timestamps:*')
=> []
```

Does this method eagerly store a job in redis for jobs in the schedule or does this only return jobs explicitly scheduled with `Resque.enqueue_at`?
Closing. `scheduled_at` only searches delayed jobs (`enqueue_at`/`enqueue_in`) and needs the exact args. Recurring schedules aren't stored as timestamps, so they never show up there.

title: Resque::NoQueueError: Jobs must be placed onto a queue.
body:
Anyone get this occasionally?

For us, we started to see this a week or so ago. It crops every couple of days, and then just keeps happening. We fix it by restarting the scheduler process. We're running on Heroku using RedisToGo (resque is basically our only use of Redis). The error is not very illuminating.

``` logs
2012-07-14T04:09:00+00:00 app[scheduler.1]: 2012-07-14 04:09:00 queueing VeniceHeartbeat (heartbeat_to_venice)
2012-07-14T04:09:00+00:00 app[scheduler.1]: 2012-07-14 04:09:00 Resque::NoQueueError: Jobs must be placed onto a queue.
```

This job runs all the time, and works well over 99% of the time. Occasionally, though, it just stops working. We have not yet verified if other scheduled jobs also fail to be scheduled.

The config entry for this:

``` yaml
heartbeat_to_venice:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  cron: "* * * * *"
  class: VeniceHeartbeat
  args:
  description: "Lets venice know we're alive"
```

Worth noting, the job absolutely specifies the `@queue` member, and this job works pretty much all the time. 

Here's some stuff out of our Gemfile.lock:

``` gemfile
GIT
  remote: git://github.com/bvandenbos/resque-scheduler
  revision: 9db9e9e2512636d31d9d9f8e0a761b74f3f43408
  specs:
    resque-scheduler (2.0.0.h)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
      redis (>= 2.0.1)         
      resque (>= 1.20.0)       
      rufus-scheduler          

   resque (1.20.0)         
```

comments.body:
either VeniceHeartbeat class itself or the yaml file must specify a queue.

In the class it's as `@queue = :venice` in the yaml it's a line as `queue: venice`

confirm you have one of those first.
Confirmed. Like I said, everything works great most of the time .

I am getting this exact same issue.

Ruby 1.9.3-p194 with resque 1.20.0

Works 99% of the time, then this particular job will throw Resque::NoQueueError when the queue is clearly defined.

Just experienced this, and after some digging around, it seems this is caused because the scheduler will try to constantize your class, and if it isn't able to, it will use it as a string.

So a call to `Resque.queue_from_class(klass)` when `klass` is a string, will return false, thus raising the error.

Solution is to load the environment (`rake environment rake:scheduler`), require your class in the `setup` step, or add the `queue` to the config file.

I'd recommend the latter option, so as to keep the scheduler process light.
@ivanyv Not sure that accounts for the symptoms. Why would that start failing after a while and not right away?

Beats me, maybe something to do with load order or unloading of modules... just shooting in the dark here.

For me it was caused by what I said in my previous comment.
I had this problem, and it ended up that I was doing queue = :foo instead of @queue = :foo in my task class.

Same issue here, I have to specify `queue: background` in the schedule.yml file.
I have `@queue = :background` in my job file.

title: Allow ignoring errors based on a certain event messages?
body:
Hi,

one of the biggest annoyances I currently experience is that, running a lot of k8s CronJob resources, multiple times a day I get this

> There is an issue with container in a pod!
> Name: name of pod
> Container: container name
> Reason: CreateContainerConfigError

However, the _actual_ reason for this is:
```
[2022-08-02 00:00:00 +0000 UTC] Scheduled Successfully assigned namespace/pod to ip-123-456-…
[2022-08-02 00:00:04 +0000 UTC] Pulled Container image "<container>" already present on machine
[2022-08-02 00:00:02 +0000 UTC] Failed Error: failed to sync configmap cache: timed out waiting for the condition
[2022-08-02 00:00:07 +0000 UTC] Created Created container container
```

> Failed Error: failed to sync configmap cache: timed out waiting for the condition

In **all** those cases, the container is started (after, what seems, a 5s timeout). In none of the observed cases the container was not started.

I truly wish it would be possible to ignore them, as you can imagine they generate quite a lot of noise.

---
As for the reason, I'm no expert, but it seems that at certain points too many jobs are being scheduled at the same time and k8s internally throttles the requests and then this happens. I'm fine with the internal throttling and rather not want to manually pick apart the jobs schedule and move them to different minutes (it's easier to comprehend when they hit at full hours, etc.)

Is this something which can be considered?

title: Add job_id to DagRun table and remove BackfillJob zombies
body: # Description Currently, we have `run_type` in the DagRun table but there's no way to determine what job created a DagRun (no 1-1 relation between DagRun and Job). This can be helpful in debugging (I think especially in the case of Scheduler HA and BackfillJobs) as this will also allow users to check which scheduler / backfill job triggered their task (now the job_id in TaskInstance is always id of LocalTaskJob). Introducing job_id may help us with making backfill runnable remotely as we will be able to clean up after jobs that failed thus reducing possible zombies. ## The problem Run: ``` airflow dags backfill -v -s 2020-10-06 example_bash_operator # once there's a process running single task, do the following: pkill -9 -f backfil ``` this will result in "zombie" DagRun and related task instance that will not be cleaned up by the scheduler (at least that's my understanding). Example: However, querying the the job table we see: So, the backfill job is still running according to Airflow state but that's not true as we killed the job 👎 ## Possible solution Link a specific job to DagRun triggered by it (using the `job_id`) and then run a process that will kill the zombies. This can be done either by: - killing a DR (and related TIs) that is in an unfinished state (running, none, scheduled, queued) but the job that was running it is in error state - killing a DR (and related TIs) that is in an unfinished state but the job that was running it didn't heartbeat for the last few minutes (configurable) Cleaning of such zombies can be easily triggered by the scheduler. I think this may bring us closer to triggering backfill via API / UI. ## Use case / motivation Introduce the relation between DagRun and Job tables and implement a process that will clean up zombies created by BackfillJobs. **Related Issues** https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/8227 Thanks to our friends from [Databand](https://databand.ai) for hinting this!

comments.body: @ashb @mik-laj I'm happy to hear what do you think

Do you have a case where it's interesting to know what job created the DagRun? (I ask because I can't think of one immediately)

Don't forget that in the case of trigger (via CLI or webserver) there is no job id to use.

I would probably suggest naming it `created_by_job_id` - it's a bit clearer what it stores then just `job_id`

> Do you have a case where it's interesting to know what job created the DagRun? (I ask because I can't think of one immediately)

I have an operator that triggers backfill job and observes that process. If the "parent" task dies (SIGKILL) then there are zombie tasks (scheduled/none state) from backfill job that are not cleaned up by anything. But that's probably an egde case + we use custom implementation of BackfillJob (that's why I was able to fix it using `DagRun.conf` for storing job_id - a hack). 

However, I think that this information can be helpful in case of multiple schedulers, for example, to find that only one of them has some problems (no idea what problems).

So, basically my suggestion is about adding not crucial information that **may** help sometimes 😄 

> I would probably suggest naming it `created_by_job_id` - it's a bit clearer what it stores then just `job_id`

+1 to this

After a discussion with @turbaszek - I think it's super useful to have this information as it allows us to do investigations on the reasons for problems and we can add more information - like we will know which scheduler created a DagRun.  I would love to get it added even for 2.0 after merging the HA change.

Additionally, this may help us with making backfill runnable remotely. ## The problem Run: ``` airflow dags backfill -v -s 2020-10-06 example_bash_operator # once there's a process running single task, do the following: pkill -9 -f backfil ``` this will result in "zombie" DagRun and related task instance that will not be cleaned up by the scheduler (at least that's my understanding). Example: However, querying the the job table we see: So, the backfill job is still running according to Airflow state but that's not true as we killed the job 👎 ## Possible solution Link a specific job to DagRun triggered by it (using the `job_id`) and then run a process that will kill the zombies. This can be done either by: - killing a DR (and related TIs) that is in an unfinished state (running, none, scheduled, queued) but the job that was running it is in error state - killing a DR (and related TIs) that is in an unfinished state but the job that was running it didn't heartbeat for the last few minutes (configurable) Cleaning of such zombies can be easily triggered by the scheduler. I think this may bring us closer to triggerin

Got it, that makes sense.

There's code in the scheduler ha branch they will kill timed out/not heartbeating SchedulerJobs - that could be extended to Backfill job too.

I'm not sure what change would be needed to detect zombie tasks from backfilled jobs, but it's a good goal I agree.
I will try to tackle it once #10956 is merged
+1 to this change, thanks @turbaszek

comments.body:
Issue is reproduced by wp.org woocommerce support team : 
https://wordpress.org/support/topic/woocommerce-adds-2-products-to-cart-because-of-redirect/
With the precision : 
"it looks like this behavior appears only when Default customer location is set to Geolocate with page caching support and Add to cart behaviors are unchecked."

I have indeed the "redirect" disabled, not the ajax action. (and no clue about this "geolocate" option)

Note that it was also reported in SO 6 years ago : https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49699928/custom-add-to-cart-url-adding-product-twice-to-the-cart-in-woocommerce-3-3-1

I can reproduce on my stock setup, no geolocation needed.


Whatever is doing the add to cart needs to be a bit late to account for redirect, otherwise the query should be deleted.

The issue here is that `WC_Form_Handler::add_to_cart_action` is running too early in `wp_loaded`, while all redirects happen on `template_redirect`.

A solution would be to switch `add_to_cart_action` and `update_cart_action` to `template_redirect`.

Doing that alone, and keeping priority on 20, would surface another issue in which doing something like `checkout?add-to-cart=27` on an empty cart would result in the item not being added and a redirect to cart.

This is because the logic that redirects empty cart is on `wc_template_redirect` is at `template_redirect:10`, so that one should be pushed further, but no further than `add_to_cart_action`, so the sequence should be:

- `canonical_redirect` from WP, happens first in `template_redirect` this should fix the `/` issue. at 10.
- `add_to_cart_action` from WC happens at `template_redirect` at 15.
- `wc_template_redirect` from WC happens at `template_redirect` at 20.

The risk is that if something is relying on running after those things might break.

Another solution would be to keep `add_to_cart_action` at 10 and keep `wc_template_redirect` but this risks race condition, though to me it's unlikely given how the code is structured: WP code will always register first, `class-wc-form-handler.php` is loaded after that, in `load-post.php` hook, and `wc_template_redirect` is in `after_setup_theme`.

Thanks for the report. I know this has been open a while, and I appreciate your patience. We're currently going through some older WooCommerce issues, identifying what still needs fixing, and tidying up what's already fixed or out of scope.

I've taken a look and marked this ready for the engineering team to pick up.

comments.body:
I've also replicated this using WC 8.6.1.

![CleanShot 2024-02-21 at 13 12 37](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/assets/14240438/1d25321e-933d-4f56-941d-ce39f2d1898f)
Still valid as of 10.9.4, moving to engineering

Hey team. 

I was able to replicate this issue on latest trunk.

When saving or publishing a coupon with a special character (like &), `WC_Post_Data::wp_insert_post_data` sanitizes the `shop_coupon` post title using `wp_filter_kses()`. KSES converts unencoded ampersands `&` to `&`, saving 'Coupon&Test' to the database. Upon reloading the page for editing, WordPress loads the post title in the edit context, which runs `esc_html()` on the already entity-encoded title. This double-encodes the title to 'Coupon&amp;Test', displaying as literal "Coupon&Test" in the input field.

To fix this we can update `WC_Post_Data::wp_insert_post_data` to sanitize coupon post titles using `wc_sanitize_coupon_code()` instead of `wp_filter_kses()`. After that we can update `wc_sanitize_coupon_code()` to recursively decode HTML entities using `html_entity_decode()` and strip HTML tags via `wp_strip_all_tags()`. This ensures ampersands are preserved raw in the database (matching how WordPress handles titles containing ampersands for other post types).

We should also update/add relevant unit tests in `WC_Meta_Box_Coupon_Data_Test` and `WC_Formatting_Functions_Test`.

Please let me know if this solution looks good. Also, could you please assign this issue to me so I can raise a PR?

Thanks!

title: Zero cost orders renewals fail generating order without proper renewal metadata and blanked "order_type"
body:

### Prerequisites

If you have a variable product with variations, and want to update the product and variations' SKU in a single CSV import, the variations are deleted, and the parent product is not updated.

> Change the SKUs to a new format, including the parent column

Noting that if you leave the parent column as the parent ID, this issue doesn't occur. SKUs can also be changed by importing the variable product(s) first then import the variations with the updated parent SKUs.

Received a report of this on 7836260-zen.

That user was able to successfully update the SKUs for all product types individually (like @rrennick described above). In this case some of their Variable products did not have SKUs (only the variations did), so they were able to update those SKUs by referencing the product ID for the Variable product in the "Parent" column.

I've taken a look and marked this ready for the engineering team to pick up. This looks to still be reproducible.

What I'm seeing: The CSV importer still resolves parent references through parse_relative_field() and aborts variations when the parent product cannot be resolved yet, so the reported parent-SKU/variation update edge case remains plausible and no trunk fix was found.

We need to make same-import parent-variation SKU updates work. Looks like there's some sort of ID remapping used, but not SKU remapping.

I investigated this further and found that the same underlying problem also affects grouped products, upsells, and cross-sells—not just variations.

When a CSV changes a product’s SKU and references that new SKU elsewhere in the same import, the importer can create a temporary product for the reference before saving the SKU change. This can cause the SKU update to fail and relationships to point to that temporary product instead.

Cleanup then deletes the temporary product. For variations, this can also delete existing variations. For grouped products, upsells, and cross-sells, the original products survive, but their saved relationships are replaced with references to temporary products that cleanup deletes. As a result, grouped items and product recommendations can disappear from the storefront.

A smaller initial fix could reject updates that would attach existing products to temporary products, preserving the existing data and reporting a row error instead. I can incorporate this fix into my open draft PR.

The above mentioned smaller fix would prevent this data loss, but would not make the requested SKU changes succeed. A complete fix needs a separate design discussion about how references should resolve across rows and import batches, while preserving existing import behavior.

title: Have pgbackrest exit silently when run against a standby node
body:
We have a two-node Patroni cluster with the backup repository on S3. To keep the setup symmetrical I would like to be able to run the same cronjob/systemd timer on both nodes, but have the backup only suceed on the primary node. Since we don't need it (and generally don't want for security), there is no password-less ssh connection between the two nodes, so each of the pgbackrest.conf files has only `pg1` configured.

At the moment, this setup fails on the standby side:
```
$ pgbackrest --stanza=prod backup
ERROR: [056]: unable to find primary cluster - cannot proceed
```

My expectation would be that there would be a way to tell pgbackrest not to do anything when invoked on a non-primary node. At the moment I'm hacking around that by asking the Patroni API if the local node is a primary:
```
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'if curl -o /dev/null -sf localhost:8008; then pgbackrest --stanza=prod --type=full --log-level-console=info backup; else echo "Not running on primary node, skipping pgbackrest"; fi'
```
I believe the functionality should be built into pgbackrest so this command line shouldn't have to be that ugly.
We aren't asking for pgbackrest to talk to the Patroni API - just connecting to the local PG instance and exiting if it's not a primary would be perfect.


A side issue here is that I can't be explicit about not wanting to backup from the primary:
```
$ pgbackrest --stanza=valantic_prod --backup-standby=n backup
ERROR: [031]: option 'backup-standby' does not allow an argument
```

Thanks for considering.

comments.body:
Hi,

Afaik, the ssh connection between PG hosts isn't needed when the repo is shared. And it can have multiple benefits to define all pg hosts in the config. [Here](https://pgstef.github.io/2020/09/04/combining_pgbackrest_and_streaming_replication.html) is an (old but still working) example just fwiw.

Backups activation in case of failover is not specific to pgBR but to any backup method. I've usually seen this handled using `pg_is_in_recovery()`. Wouldn't that be an option in your case ?

To be honest, I wouldn't be in favor of silently failing because we ask for a backup and we can't take one. Its imho best to not ask for the backup to avoid false positives... But perhaps @dwsteele will have other ideas :-)

Kind regards,

Afaict the ssh connection is required at the moment because pgbackrest is `unable to find primary cluster`, which it should not require.

It doesn't have to skip the backup silently, I'd be fine by some `skip_backup_on_standby = true` option.

`pg_is_in_recovery()` would be the thing to look for, yes. I wasn't putting that in the OP since I assumed everyone already knew that :).

> It doesn't have to skip the backup silently, I'd be fine by some skip_backup_on_standby = true option.

Yeah, it would need to be a new option. It would not be OK to change how the current option works.

I'm OK with this idea in principal, but I'd like to think about it a bit in case there is a better way to go about it.

> ERROR: [031]: option 'backup-standby' does not allow an argument

What you want here is `--no-backup-standby`. We are also planning to make `--backup-standby=n` work now that `getopt_long()` limitations are no longer an issue.
Shouldn't this be labeled as "enhancement" rather than "question"?
Everything starts as a question and we update when we decide for sure that it will be an enhancement. Just never got to this one.

Is there any update on it? Having a symmetric setup for a replication pair and only running backups on the primary strikes me as a valid use-case, and it seems to be really complicated with pgbackrest

No update. The feature looks viable but we have not had time to schedule it yet.

You are welcome to put together a patch yourself.

title: Memory-leak related to the resourcetotelemetry codepath?
body:
### Component(s)

exporter/prometheusremotewrite, pkg/resourcetotelemetry

### What happened?

## Description

We're troubleshooting an issue where _a single `otel-collector-...` pod out of a group begins to turn away metrics because the `memorylimiter` is tripped. In this situation, we have dozens or hundreds of clients pushing `otlp` metrics (prometheus collected, but over the otlp grpc exporter) to multiple `otel-collector-...` pods. The metrics are routed with the `loadbalancer` exporter using `routing_key: resource`.

The behavior we see is that _one_ collector suddenly starts running out of memory and being limited .. while the other collectors are using half or even less  memory to process the same number of events. Here's graphs of the ingestion and the success rate:

![image](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/assets/768067/6ddb16e3-39d1-4ada-ba5a-d2c8534e9fa7)

The two dips in the `Percentage of Metrics Accepted by Receiver` graphs are _different_ pods in a StatefulSet. Here's the graph of actual memory usage of these three pods:

![image](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/assets/768067/b47efac5-650a-40e0-87ca-c2934e127bb8)

In the first dip - from 8:30AM->9:30AM, I manually restarted the pod to recover it. It's fine now ... but a few hours later, a different one of the pods becomes overloaded. Grabbing a HEAP dump from the `pprof` endpoint on a "good" and "bad" pod shows some stark differences:

**Bad Pod Pprof**: [otel-collector-metrics-processor-collector-0.pb.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/15569864/otel-collector-metrics-processor-collector-0.pb.gz)
![image](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/assets/768067/123cd57c-a367-4b29-a87a-c7b9de0cbf03)

**Good Pod Pprof**: [otel-collector-metrics-processor-collector-1.pb.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/15569867/otel-collector-metrics-processor-collector-1.pb.gz)
![image](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/assets/768067/c0616539-2df6-4ec7-a49c-8943840cec43)

I should note that this isn't remotely our largest environment - and these pods are handling ~12-15k datapoints/sec, while our larger environments are doing ~20k/sec/pod... so this doesn't feel like a fundamental scale issue. All pods are sized the same across all of our environments.

### Collector version

v0.101.0

# Community Note

**Voting for Prioritization**

* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original post to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request.
* Please see our [prioritization guide](https://hashicorp.github.io/terraform-provider-aws/prioritization/) for information on how we prioritize.
* Please **do not** leave "+1" or other comments that do not add relevant new information or questions, they generate extra noise for issue followers and do not help prioritize the request.

**Volunteering to Work on This Issue**

* If you are interested in working on this issue, please leave a comment.
* If this would be your first contribution, please review the [contribution guide](https://hashicorp.github.io/terraform-provider-aws/).

According to the [AWS Backup Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/whatisbackup.html), EBS cold storage archive tier is indeed not supported in the GovCloud regions:

> Amazon EBS cold storage archive tier is not available in is not currently available in China (Beijing), China (Ningxia), AWS GovCloud (US-East) and AWS GovCloud (US-West) Regions.

Thus the AWS API is failing as expected.
But I'm not using the cold storage tier. Why is it expected that if  I pass false to an option related to cold storage, the API will fail?

In the earlier comment I was just making note of the EBS code storage support statement more explicitly. I was still digging into this interesting problem.

I believe that the conversion is a result how the Terraform Plugin SDK is handling schema attributes. hashicorp/terraform-plugin-sdk#817 describes the problem and a seeming lack of support for a tri-state boolean (any primitive value for that matter). There are some workarounds but I am not sure which one is the most appropriate architecturally speaking. Terraform is highly discouraging the use of [`d.getOkExists`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-sdk/v2/helper/schema#ResourceData.GetOkExists) but also not providing an alternative. The next best thing is [`d.GetRawConfig`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-sdk/v2/helper/schema#ResourceData.GetRawConfig) but it's considered experimental. Either way, it would also be interesting to see how these can be used in the context of configuration blocks.

I've also seen in some other AWS resource code that related attributes are used to determine the setting. For example, one could pass in `opt_in_to_archive_for_supported_resources` only if `cold_storage_after` is set (or > 0) during expansion. But this doesn't feel exactly right.

Just leaving some research notes here - I think we'll need a core contributor to chime in.
Hey @tmccombs 👋 Thanks for another great bug report! Did this come up after upgrading to 5.33.0? Looking at whether this needs a regression label.
I don't know if it is a regression, this is the first time I've tried creating this resource in a GovCloud region.

Related #34994

☝️ With that (and the more recent comments on it), labeling this a regression. @tmccombs with that in mind, if you happen to be able to use 5.32.1, you should be able to work around this for now.

ok thanks. 

Another thought on this: 

During creation, if the value is `false` set the `OptInToArchiveForSupportedResources` parameter to nil instead.

During update, if the value is `false` and the previous value was also `false` (or nil) , then don't set `OptInToArchiveForSupportedResources`. (or set it to nil).

You are providing a timezone via environment variable and by mounting your servers timezone into the container. Any chance those two are different? Maybe that could cause weird behavior? I'd remove one of those regardless.

Removing the volume mount made no difference.

WUD ran at midnight last night which is the same time a script kicks off that runs the plextraktsync container.  The container ran for about 3 mins.  It appears that every time a new container comes on line, goes offline, or is removed, WUD is performing a new scan and ignoring the cron schedule.  The WUD log below shows it knows what time it is supposed to run, but seems to have ignored the schedule and ran anyway.

```

>  It appears that every time a new container comes on line, goes offline, or is removed, WUD is performing a new scan

That's likely because of the [`WUD_WATCHER_{watcher_name}_WATCHEVENTS`](https://fmartinou.github.io/whats-up-docker/#/configuration/watchers/) property.
If you want wud to scan only with the cron, you need to disable it. Can you try?

That seems to have made an impact.  When `WUD_WATCHER_{watcher_name}_WATCHEVENTS` is not set and defaults to true, WUD scans when a container is removed and readded.  It does not when it is set to false.

I run 100+ containers on the host and had 43,000+ line items show up in the docker pull request report in a 24 hour period. Ubuntu has a history of shipping things in combinations that break things in ways you couldn't encounter outside of their releases, so if I see a crash report from Ubuntu with mismatched kernel/userland versions, I'm going to suggest you try the vanilla release.

Hi @carolframen - thanks for the report.

I know this has been open for a long time, and I appreciate your patience. We're currently going through some older WooCommerce issues, identifying what still needs fixing, and tidying up what's already fixed or out of scope.

I've taken a look and marked this ready for the engineering team to pick up.

What I'm seeing: The order-again path still reconstructs variation data from order item metadata and stores it directly on the cart item. Cart display then formats variation values by looking up a taxonomy term slug; if the reconstructed key/value does not match the taxonomy lookup path, WooCommerce can display the raw slug. I found no open PR or changelog evidence that specifically fixes this global-attribute order-again behavior.

Hi! I checked this against current trunk with a regression fixture using a long global attribute and term value. It reproduces the raw slug when I restore the old mapping, but passes on trunk. The variation normalization merged in #61344 appears to cover this case, so this may now be resolved.
I believe it's a partial solve so keeping this open for engineering to have a look. Thanks for following up! Kudos.

I've checked this on a local Studio site using the long global attribute name and values containing spaces, numbers, and special characters from the report. After using **Order again**, the values display correctly in both the classic cart and Cart block.

This is covered by [#61344](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/pull/61344), which normalised variation attributes when rebuilding the cart from an order. Restoring the old mapping reproduces the raw slugs.

**Old mapping:**

![Classic cart showing raw attribute slugs](https://embed.uploads.sh/mikejolley/gh/woocommerce/woocommerce/issues/47808/order-again-pre-61344.webp)

**Current trunk, classic cart:**

![Classic cart showing correct attribute names and values](https://embed.uploads.sh/mikejolley/gh/woocommerce/woocommerce/issues/47808/order-again-trunk.webp)

**Current trunk, Cart block:**

![Cart block showing correct attribute names and values](https://embed.uploads.sh/mikejolley/gh/woocommerce/woocommerce/issues/47808/order-again-trunk-block-cart.webp)

Closing this as fixed. I couldn't reproduce a remaining issue with the reported examples; if there's a case the fix doesn't cover, please share the attribute names, values, and steps so we can investigate.

已在 v1.4.x 修复，抱歉拖了这么久。

你和 @sloganlau 遇到的「每 3 个月就要重装一次」有两个叠加的根因：

1. **续期时 acme 校验路径不可达**。旧版靠按行号 `sed` 临时改写 Nginx 配置来放行 `/.well-known/acme-challenge/`，平时 80 端口对该路径是无条件 301 到 https 的，续期只能靠 CA 跟随重定向落到 443 才侥幸成功——你日志里的 `Fetching https://.../.well-known/... Connection refused` 正是这一步失败。现在该 location 在 Nginx 中常驻，签发与续期都不再依赖 Xray 监听哪个端口。
2. **续期成功也没用**。`--install-cert` 在脚本里被多处调用，后一次会覆盖前一次记录的 `--reloadcmd`，一旦被清空，续期后既不会修正 `/ssl` 权限也不会重启 Xray，Xray 仍在用旧证书。现在 `--reloadcmd` 收敛为单一入口，并在其中一并 `chown` 与 `systemctl restart xray`。

另外 v1.4.0 起 acme.sh 安装后会执行 `--upgrade --auto-upgrade`，避免老版本因 CA API 变动而续期失败。

顺带回答你的疑问：证书有效期 90 天，acme.sh 的 cron 会在到期前自动续期，你 2 月签发、5 月失效，正是自动续期失败所致，判断没错。

请更新脚本后重装一次（或手动跑一次菜单 36 强制续期），后续应当不再需要人工干预：

```bash
wget -N --no-check-certificate -q -O install.sh "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wulabing/Xray_onekey/main/install.sh" && chmod +x install.sh && bash install.sh
```

至于 `Failed to stop firewalld.service: Unit firewalld.service not loaded.` 这类提示，是脚本在逐个尝试关闭各类防火墙，系统没装该防火墙就会这么提示，属正常现象，与证书问题无关。

title: Prevent multiple parallel --renew runs on same domain
body: Running `acme.sh --renew` multiple times in parallel may break the `$domain.conf` file and prevent future runs from succeeding. We faced this issue after a manual and a cron-triggered run happened at the same time, mangling the `$domain.conf` file. It would be nice if `acme.sh` could prevent this from happening, e.g. by detecting parallel runs and exiting early with an error if a conflict is detected. Perhaps some per-domain lock as explained here: https://www.putorius.net/lock-files-bash-scripts.html

* Mod 1: Debugging (xtrace)
  `acme.sh` 1st line `#!/bin/bash -x`
* Mod 2: Native FreeBSD interpreter (bash->sh)
  `acme.sh` 1st line `#!/bin/sh`

**Conditions**
* Cond 1: Simple call (no redirection)
  `su -m acme -c '/mnt/dsk/services/acme/acme.sh --cron --test --home /mnt/dsk/services/acme'`
* Cond 2: Call with STDOUT to file (`>file`)

  `su -m acme -c '/mnt/dsk/services/acme/acme.sh --cron --test --home /mnt/dsk/services/acme' > /mnt/dsk/services/acme/debug-acme.log 2>&1`

**Test results**
||orig|xtrace|bash->sh
---|---|---|---
no redirection|SIGPIPE error|Not executed|No error
`>file`|No error, but cert in `file`|Not executed, empty `file`|No error, but cert in `file`
`>file 2>&1`|No error, but cert in `file`|No error, but cert in `file`|No error, but cert in `file`

**Assumptions**
It looks as if `acme.sh` has an error with the output file descriptors at some point. And `SIGPIPE` error appears for the `bash` interpreter only, while for native FreeBSD `sh` this error does not exist.

@Neilpang 
I did some more tests to further investigate `acme.sh` strange behavior in XigmaNAS custom FreeBSD kernel environment. This time I used `/dev/null` redirection and two options for calling `acme.sh` using `su` and `sudo`.

**Conditions**
* Cond 1: Call with `su` and redirect `acme.sh`
  `su -m acme -c '/mnt/dsk/services/acme/acme.sh --cron --test --home /mnt/dsk/services/acme > /dev/null'`
* Cond 2: Call with `su` and redirect `su`
  `su -m acme -c '/mnt/dsk/services/acme/acme.sh --cron --test --home /mnt/dsk/services/acme' > /dev/null`
* Cond 3: Call with `sudo` and redirect `acme.sh`
  `sudo -u acme sh -c '/mnt/dsk/services/acme/acme.sh --cron --test --home /mnt/dsk/services/acme > /dev/null'`
* Cond 4: Call with `sudo` and redirect `sudo`
  `sudo -u acme sh -c '/mnt/dsk/services/acme/acme.sh --cron --test --home /mnt/dsk/services/acme' > /dev/null` 

**Test results**
||su|sudo
---|---|---
no redirection|SIGPIPE error|SIGPIPE error
`acme.sh >`|No error|No error
`su/sudo >`|No error|No error

**Notes**
Additional info about test conditions specific to XigmaNAS FreeBSD instance.
1. Error after server start and call via `cron`.
1. No error if `acme.sh` runs in CLI.
1. Error after `cron` **restart in CLI** and call via `cron`.
1. No error after `cron` **restart in XigmaNAS webUI** and call via `cron`.

@Neilpang
After some discussion with XigmaNAS development team, it turns out the root cause of the issue is as follows.
1. FreeBSD local mail subsystem is not configured in XigmaNAS system by design.
1. At run time `acme.sh` script outputs some data (cert content) to STDOUT, which is not expected with `--cron` command line option.
1. System `cron` tries to send any of STDOUT and STDERR `acme.sh` output via `mail`, except it's redirected.
1. Because local mail is not configured, the `mail` utility, invoked by `cron`, dies while script is still running, which causes broken pipe (SIGPIPE) error.

A solid workaround is to redirect `acme.sh` script output to `>/dev/null 2>&1`.

It seems this issue is specific to XigmaNAS system only, otherwise there would be numerous issue reports in different use cases.
Closing as stale: no activity for over 18 months. If this still applies on the current release, please open a new issue with the `--debug 2` log.
Not a bug: reporter traced it to XigmaNAS lacking a local mail system, so cron's mail pipe dies and SIGPIPEs acme.sh; redirecting the cron output is the fix.

title: Password reset flow fails if cookie header is SameSite=Strict
body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I have carried out troubleshooting steps and I believe I have found a bug.
- [X] I have searched for similar bugs in both open and closed issues and cannot find a duplicate.

### Describe the bug

For a user to reset their password, they first fill out the "Lost Password" form which generates an email containing a link in the format:

`example.com/my-account/lost-password/?key=#&id=#`

Following this link then sets a cookie `wp-resetpass-COOKIEHASH` before redirecting to 

`/my-account/lost-password/?show-reset-form=true&action`

Within the `lost_password()` method of the `WC_Shortcode_My_Account` class, it performs a check for this cookie before rendering the password reset form. If the cookie check fails, the user is shown the initial lost password form instead.

If cookies are set to SameSite=Strict, and the user follows the password reset link from a webmail client or Slack, then the cookie fails to set, the cookie check in show_password() fails and the user is shows the lost password form again.

In order to comply with OWasp standards and pass a PCI scan it became necessary to add the `SameSite=Lax` or `SameSite=Strict` parameter to all Cookies on sites because otherwise those sites will fail their PCI scans. We followed best practice and set this to Strict which is ultimately what is causing this issue. 

### Expected behavior

The site should be allowed to use SameSite=Strict without this password reset flow failing.

### Actual behavior

Explained above.

### Steps to reproduce

Set cookies to use strict mode

Header edit Set-Cookie (.*)$ $1;SameSite=Strict;HttpOnly
Header always edit Set-Cookie (.*)$ $1;SameSite=Strict;HttpOnly

Perform a password reset, using a webmail client rather than a desktop client to follow the reset link.

title: Checkout Block gives generic try-again error after order created and paid but email fails
body:
### Prerequisites - [X] I have carried out troubleshooting steps and I believe I have found a bug. - [X] I have searched for similar bugs in both open and closed issues and cannot find a duplicate. ### Describe the bug We're using the new WooCommerce Checkout Block here:
[https://bestchinesemedicines.com/checkout/?add-to-cart=23849]() We had a severe problem recently when our email integration failed. We use the Zoho Mail plugin. Zoho hit an email send limit and started blocking transactional emails. They tell us to use their Zeptomail service instead, but separately that has been a battle. The email trouble did not result in a 500 error but it did somehow die after the orders came in and were paid and set to Processing. Customers saw a generic error message to try again later. They did. So they ended up with 2, 3, 4, 5 different paid orders of the same product. Each time they tried again, they got a duplicate order and the same generic error message. They never received the email confirmation due to the email crash. I certainly blame Zoho Mail and its plugin for the initial problem. However, there's a vulnerability here with the new Checkout Block that needs to be addressed. We cannot be telling customers that their order failed when it in fact did not. I foresee various email routing plugins and other things hooking into the post payment parts of the Store API checkout flow that can trigger this generic checkout error, misleading customers. ### Expected behavior I expect checkout to either be fine since the order was, or to let the customer know that there was a problem but their order may have gone in and to check their accounts or email customer service. ### Actual behavior Customers see a generic error message to try again later. They did. So they ended up with 2, 3, 4, 5 different paid orders of the same product. Each time they tried again, they got a duplicate order and were charged accordingly. ## Connector Configuration

Here are the main configuration parameters to keep in mind:

### `host`
The IP address or DNS name of your AS400 server.

### `port`
This depends on how your AS400 is configured:

- `449`: Default port for the **database server** (used by JDBC via JT400).
- `8470`: Used for **encrypted connections** (SSL/TLS).
- `8471`: Alternative for **unencrypted connections**, depending on your setup.
- `446`: Legacy port for **DDM (Distributed Data Management)** — rarely used today.

### `database`
The schema name you want to synchronize.

### `tables` (optional)
List of tables to synchronize, separated by a pipe character `|`.  
If this field is **not filled**, **no tables will be detected**.

---

## Creating a Custom Connector

For more **flexibility** or to enable **automatic table discovery**, you may want to build your own custom connector.

title: Card payment options are not available in multi-currency store when the account has a different default currency
body:
**Describe the bug**

> Testing Tap to Pay: After setting up TTP on my iPhone, I was invited to test it out with a $0.50 payments. However, IPP/TTP was not an option on the payment screen.

This issue is broader and affects all card payment (Card Reader, TTP) options and payment flows. If the store supports `Multi-Currency` and the account we use in the app has a different `Default Currency` set in Store's settings, then card payment options are not available. However, the Order itself indicates that it's being created with default store currency so it's not immediately clear why the options are unavailable.

**To Reproduce**

#### Before testing

1. Set up a site with WooPayments, `US` location and `USD` currency
3. Go to `Payments -> Settings`, scroll down to `Advanced Settings` and `Enable Multi-Currency`
4. Go to `Settings -> WooCommerce -> Multi-currency`, add additional currency and enable `Automatically switch customers to their local currency if it has been enabled`
5. Open your store on the browser, go to My Account, (yourstore.com/my-account/) and log into your account
6. Open Account details and change `Default currency` to something different from `USD`

#### TTP Payment setup flow

1. Open Woo app and log into the same account and site
2. Menu
3. Payments
4. Set Up Tap to Pay on iPhone
5. Try a Payment
7. Take Payment ($0.50)
8. Notice there're no 'Card Reader' and 'Tap to Pay on iPhone' option
9.  Change `Default Currency` in `yourstore.com/my-account/` 'Account details' tab back to `USD`
10. Repeat the steps, and notice Card Reader' and 'Tap to Pay on iPhone' option are available

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4b411ed-a32b-499a-828a-2b151809f528

#### Order Creation flow

1. Open Woo app and log into the same account and site
2. Order
3. Add Products
4. Notice the price is shown in dollars
5. 'Collect Payment'
6. Notice now the total is shown in a customer `Default currency`
10. Notice there're no 'Card Reader' and 'Tap to Pay on iPhone' option
11.  Change `Default Currency` in `yourstore.com/my-account/` 'Account details' tab back to `USD`
12. Repeat the steps, and notice Card Reader' and 'Tap to Pay on iPhone' option are available

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6852ca4-01dc-479c-bdf8-b8ab48ea98d6

**Investigation**

TPP options are not shown since `orderIsEligibleForCardPresentPayment` call fails due to ineligible currency. It happens when `Order.currency` is different from default WooCommerce country/currency settings which determine TPP eligiblity and supported currencies. This issue only occurs when Multi-Currency settings are enabled (`Payments > Settings > Advanced settings`) and configured `WooCommerce -> Settings -> Multi-Currency`.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e93345a2-4818-4870-9d0b-03442df8fe35)

And customer whose account matches the account used in the app has a different default currency:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9d463a3-18c0-4abf-b537-b9306ebf3e43)

**Screenshots**

|               |              |              |
|---------------|--------------|--------------|
| ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81c2f4d0-461f-4f29-9a00-376b7a2730e7) | ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7acfce4b-6c49-491b-8755-c53401ce9e32) | ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/797aa175-bcd0-4177-9154-a637abef8362) |

**Expected behavior**

The expected behavior is not clear. A few options:

- API should ignore Customer `default currency` settings when the account that is calling the API matches the Customer and always use primary store currency
- The app should always explicitly set the default store currency as order currency, matching the behavior of WP-Admin
- The app should use `Order.currency` instead of `Store's Currency Settings` when possible, to indicate correctly that the order is being created with a different currency. Righ

comments.body: Thanks for reporting! 👍 <!-- generated_by_dangermattic -->

So far, I haven't been able reproduce the issue.

When this issue happens, both the 'Tap to Pay' and 'Card Reader' options are not visible in the 'Payment Methods view'.

The visibility of these options is controlled by the `PaymentMethodsViewModel.updateCardPaymentVisibility()` method.

From code it can happen for two reasons:
- `CardPresentPaymentsConfiguration` `isSupportedCountry` is false.
- `OrderCardPresentPaymentEligibilityStore` `orderIsEligibleForCardPresentPayment` is false

However if `CardPresentPaymentsConfiguration` `isSupportedCountry` is false, then TPP setup options shouldn't be visible in the first place. Therefore, that only leaves the option of `orderIsEligibleForCardPresentPayment` returning false.

> Therefore, that only leaves the option of `orderIsEligibleForCardPresentPayment` returning false.

I confirmed that's what is happening and it's because `isCurrencyEligibleForCardPayment(cardPresentPaymentsConfiguration:)` returns false. For some reason, the `currency` on the order is `GBP` even though the store uses `USD` and the "Take Payment" screen shows a dollar sign for the $0.50 amount.

Thanks, @rachelmcr! Maybe some preferences are coming from the locale and some from the store settings 🤔 . I'll check that.

Update:

For that to happen `Order` needs to arrive with currency set to `GBP` from the backend.

@rachelmc, do you know if multi-currency settings affect Order currencies in the app? I tried to look for reasons that you have a different Order currency from WooCommerce currency but no luck so far.

Aha! I thought that only affected web customers, but the "Automatically switch customers to their local currency" setting matches the issue we're seeing with the currency on these test orders. I tried disabling multi-currency (in Payments > Settings > Advanced settings on the store) and then tried testing TTP in the app, and this time it worked! So that's likely the cause.

Note: I'd guess if we explicitly set the currency on the order created in the app, that could work around this issue. But it's also probably a low impact issue (given that I'd expect most merchants are geolocated in the same place as their store's main currency setting).

Multi-currency issues manifest when creating an order on the web with one currency and then reopening it on the app.

title: [BUG] Start Script tmux Syntax Error - Centos 7
body:
## User Story

Essentially upon install of a fresh Valheim server (I haven't tried anything else recently) on Centos 7 I was met with a error on launch coming in the form of a tmux syntax error. I have found a couple fixes but all require manual intervention (Error):

```bash
[ FAIL ] Starting vhserver: Unable to start Valheim Server
[ FAIL ] Starting vhserver: Unable to start Valheim Server: tmux error:
```

## Basic info

* **Distro:** [Centos 7 Core]
* **Game:** [Valheim]
* **Command:** [Start]
* **LinuxGSM version:** [v21.2.1]

## Further Information

Upon a fresh install while setting up a test server and a ansible script to deploy it among other things at the end of troubleshooting and tweaking my scripts I was was left with the installed valhiem server on a fresh Centos 7 install.
I went to run start before going any further in setting up cron jobs or anything like that and was left with an error on start:

```bash
[valheim@****** ~]$ ./vhserver start
[ FAIL ] Starting vhserver: Unable to start Valheim Server
[ FAIL ] Starting vhserver: Unable to start Valheim Server: tmux error:

Command
=================================
tmux new-session -d -s "vhserver" " ./valheim_server.x86_64 -name 'Valheim Server' -password  -port 2456 -world vhserver -public 1 -savedir '/var/opt/valheim/.config/unity3d/IronGate/Valheim'"

Error
=================================
usage: new-session [-AdDP] [-F format] [-n window-name] [-s session-name] [-t target-session] [-x width] [-y height] [command]
0
```
After looking around for a bit and wraping around the steps to get through to that point I started compairing the function/command_start.sh to one on a different server and found that it was functional and the new version was not.

The issue being on line 75:
`tmux new-session -d -x "${sessionwidth}" -y "${sessionheight}" -s "${sessionname}" ${preexecutable} ${executable} ${startparameters} 2> "${lgsmlogdir}/.${selfname}-tmux-error.tmp"`

needing double quotes around the `${preexecutable} ${executable} ${startparameters}` variables that were removed in a commit 9 days ago for incident #3239 with commit 3d39604 for something that looks similar but the reverse.

Ironically I get success when I add it back so I am not sure if it is just a me thing or if it is a syntax issue. as I would understand it as everything after the `-s "${sessionname}"` in tmux would need to be a single command but I haven't dove that far into troubleshooting for the edge cases.

`tmux new-session -d -x "${sessionwidth}" -y "${sessionheight}" -s "${sessionname}" "${preexecutable} ${executable} ${startparameters}" 2> "${lgsmlogdir}/.${selfname}-tmux-error.tmp"`

It currently isn't impacting me as I can just reuse an old verions or template a version with quotes but it might help some other soul in the mean time.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behaviour:
1. Deploy a Centos 7 VM 
1. Mount App Directory (I use /var/opt)
1. Update Packages and Install Deps
1. Create App User with a home in App mount (/var/opt/valheim)
1. Curl install scripts down and run (Attempted with auto-install and regular install)
1. Run server start (./vhserver start)

## Expected behaviour

Post installation start even with default settings to start without error.

## Have not tried

1. Copying the install steps word for word as I usually try to avoid putting apps in /home if possible.
2. Trying a different distro like Ubuntu/Debian.
3. Tried to echo the syntax as it is when running the command without double quotes.
4. Tried on a currently functional server *Edit*
5. Moving the quotes to be around ` ${executable} ${startparameters}` leave pre exec  out*Edit*

Again I suspect this is a me thing as the commit would have been 9 days ago and there doesn't seem to be any reports other then myself and the Arma report yesterday but that seems to be slightly different. Feel free to close this if you want and I'll try to help betw

title: Dagster RunConfig conversion to config dictionary fails if underlying Config has field called 'keys'
body:
### What's the issue?

I was updating an existing schedule to use Dagster's RunConfig syntax when creating the RunRequest rather than an {"ops": ...} dictionary and during the automatic conversion of the RunConfig to a config dictionary, Dagster would throw "'list' object is not callable" errors which was quite confusing.

The underlying config object was roughly equivalent to

AConfig(Config)
    keys: list[str]

Changing the field name from "keys" to basically anything else resolved the issue and had Dagster correctly yielding the RunRequests with no other changes.




### What did you expect to happen?

I expected that the schedule would be able to correctly convert a valid RunConfig object regardless of whether one of the underlying Config objects has a field called 'keys'. Alternatively, error handling providing a more descriptive message than 'list' object is not callable would also have been a good outcome.

### How to reproduce?

from dagster import (
    schedule,
    RunRequest,
    ScheduleEvaluationContext,
    RunConfig,
    job,
    op,
    Config,
)


class BasicConfig(Config):
    keys: list[str]


@op
def basic_op(config: BasicConfig):
    print(config.keys)


@job
def basic_job():
    basic_op()


@schedule(
    job=basic_job,
    cron_schedule="00 17 * * *",
    execution_timezone="America/Toronto",
    name="aum_schedule",
)
def basic_schedule(context: ScheduleEvaluationContext):
    run_config = RunConfig(ops={"basic_op": BasicConfig(keys=[])})
    return RunRequest(run_key="", run_config=run_config)

Running this schedule will raise the error mentioned above.

### Dagster version

1.9.3

### Deployment type

None

### Deployment details

Should not be relevant, even running using build_schedule_context() in a local pass is enough to invoke.

### Additional information

_No response_

### Message from the maintainers

Impacted by this issue? Give it a 👍! We factor engagement into prioritization.
By submitting this issue, you agree to follow Dagster's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/blob/master/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

comments.body: Using "keys" as a field name is likely conflicting with Dagster's internal handling of configurations, treating "keys" as a special method or property. I'd generally advise against using names that are commonly used as method names in Python, such as keys, items, values, etc.

> Using "keys" as a field name is likely conflicting with Dagster's internal handling of configurations, treating "keys" as a special method or property. I'd generally advise against using names that are commonly used as method names in Python, such as keys, items, values, etc.

Yeah that totally makes sense and I don't think Config objects need to support them as valid fieldnames, but it might be helpful to note somewhere in the documentation that some of these names will cause issues if used as object attributes.

title: Automate import/export
body:
In all of my projects I have set connections that would be useful for entire team to use. I now export all of them and put on share, then they import them.

It would be great to simplify importing/exporting projects via command line. Here are some ideas of how this could work:

```sh
#export all projects with drivers
dbeaver --export --projects '*' --with-drivers -o ~/dbeaver.dbp

#export only selected projects
dbeaver --export --projects 'General, ProjectXYZ' -o ~/dbeaver.dbp 

#export only projects starting with Project_ preffix and General.
dbeaver --export --projects 'Project_*, General' -o ~/dbeaver.dbp 

#import all projects from dbp file, overwrite any existing projects
dbeaver --import --projects '*' --with-drivers -f ~/dbever.dbp  --overwrite

#import all projects from dbp file, use specific prefix for project names
dbeaver --import --projects '*' --with-drivers -f ~/dbever.dbp  --prefix 'share_' -overwrite

#import all projects from dbp file, map input names to given names
dbeaver --import --projects 'XYZ:MY_XYZ' --with-drivers -f ~/dbever.dbp 
```

This would allow database manager to put this in a cron job and export to common share or git repository for others/new memebers. Others could use cron job or script to sync, and with given prefix to import into specific 'namespace' so that their own stuff doesn't get changed (so that they can use copy/paste or some other method to update their local projects).

Saved passwords would become a problem then if they are not to be shared. Currently connection fails if password is not given but dbeaver could prompt for it. This applies to scenario in which domain login (OS Auth) is not used.

comments.body: This is similar to #1271 (additional command line processing).

Its not exactly similar, although it would be a nice addition.

I somehow missed _Open Project from File System_ option. Now, I saved project to shared location and each developer can open it from there. Each developer now can add bookmarks, sql files and new connections. Do you consider there to be any problem with that approach if they work on different things for example ? So far I observed the following:

* Working on same SQL files wont be a problem since dbeaver monitors for changes. 
* To see bookmarks of others F5 is required in running projects.
* Changing connection properties requires F5.

All looks like something I can work with. Perhaps automatic refreshing on entire project would be nice to have among options or notification about file system changes.

I'd propose to put your shared project under some version control (git, svn, etc). Otherwise eventually there will be many conflicts in SQL scripts and other artifacts.

You can install version control plugins thru Eclipse Marketplace in EE version or use external tools (like Tortoise) in CE version.

This feature (opening external project) is already there.
Switch to Projects view->Create new project (in toolbar)->Set location of external project.

body:
### Prerequisites

### Describe the bug

Fatal error when executing wp-cron jobs via WP-CLI.

```
$ wp cron event run --due-now
[snip]
Executed the cron event 'pum_daily_scheduled_events' in 0.022s.
Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to a member function get_date_created() on null in MYSITE/wp-content/plugins/woocommerce/packages/woocommerce-admin/src/Notes/CustomizingProductCatalog.php:52

### Expected behavior

No fatal error.

### Actual behavior

Fatal error.

### Steps to reproduce

Unfortunately I am not sure exactly what it is about this site that causes this issue. However, here is the relevant code from `CustomizingProductCatalog.php`:

```php
$query = new \WC_Product_Query(
    array(
        'limit'    => 1,
        'paginate' => true,
        'status'   => array( 'publish' ),
        'orderby'  => 'post_date',

);

$products = $query->get_products();

// we need at least 1 product.
if ( 0 === $products->total ) {

}

$product           = $products->products[0];
$created_timestamp = $product->get_date_created()->getTimestamp();
```

The last line is the line that fails.

wp> $products = $query->get_products();

You can see that whatever product is returned from the database is then filtered out by other code. I know this can happen with the base `WP_Query` (for example for password-protected posts).

title: Disabling tcp btl causes issues for rdma osc when running IMB-RMA
body:
Thank you for taking the time to submit an issue!

## Background information

### What version of Open MPI are you using? (e.g., v3.0.5, v4.0.2, git branch name and hash, etc.)

4.1.1
Master nightly tarball from Nov. 4th

### Describe how Open MPI was installed (e.g., from a source/distribution tarball, from a git clone, from an operating system distribution package, etc.)

from release tarballs; only the `--prefix=...` configure parameter was used

### Please describe the system on which you are running

* Operating system/version: based on RHEL 7
* Computer hardware: Intel
* Network type: Mellanox (ConnectX-5) with UCX 1.9.0

-----------------------------

## Details of the problem

I normally disable the tcp btl in order to have jobs fail with an obvious error if there is a problem with the high speed interconnect's communication library. This way I know when optimal performance isn't happening. I have found, however, that disabling the tcp btl causes the rdma osc to cause problems when trying to run `IMB-RMA` (Intel MPI Benchmark's RMA). When that is done, a message like this occurs:

```
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
At least one pair of MPI processes are unable to reach each other for
MPI communications.  This means that no Open MPI device has indicated
that it can be used to communicate between these processes.  This is
an error; Open MPI requires that all MPI processes be able to reach
each other.  This error can sometimes be the result of forgetting to
specify the "self" BTL.

  Process 1 ([[9281,1],4]) is on host: ko002
  Process 2 ([[9281,1],0]) is on host: ko001
  BTLs attempted: self sm

Your MPI job is now going to abort; sorry.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

This happens in both 4.1.1 and the nightly tarball from Nov 4th for master. If I enable the tcp btl, or disable the rdma osc, `IMB-RMA` runs just fine. I can also force the use of the ucx osc, and that seems to get `IMB-RMA` to work as well.

I am currently running `IMB-RMA` like the following:
```shell
# Fails
$> mpirun --map-by ppr:1:node --mca btl '^tcp' ./IMB-RMA
# Works
$> mpirun --map-by ppr:1:node --mca btl '^tcp' --mca osc '^rdma' ./IMB-RMA
$> mpirun --map-by ppr:1:node --mca btl '^tcp' --mca osc ucx ./IMB-RMA
```

In all cases, the ucx osc component is chosen, at least according to the output when I use `--mca osc_base_verbose 100`. So, it seems that the initialization of the rdma osc component has issues when the tcp btl is missing. Is this expected?

Thanks,
David

comments.body: In talking with @hppritcha, this may be about the osc rdma component complaining about the lack of an inter-node btl being available. `ompi_info` for the master nightly tarball does list a uct btl, but that component is not referenced in the error message. I'll have to see if the uct btl is being tried at all at runtime.

According to the verbose btl output, the uct btl is attempted, but init of it failed:

```
select: init of component uct returned failure
```

So, if I turn off tcp, then there really are no btls for inter-node transport available. I am not able to figure out why the uct btl fails to init, however, so I don't know what else to try to test the theory of no inter-node btls being available as the root cause of the error when the osc rdma component is allowed to init.
Hey, UCT fails to enable because we don't set a default memory domain (this is changing). I have been out of the loop on LANL systems for some time. Is this a new system with Mellanox HCAs? mlx5?
@hjelmn, this machine has been around for three or four years... It has Mellanox ConnectX-5 cards. `lspci` says the card is in the MT27800 family.
Try with ```--mca btl_uct_memory_domains mlx5_0,mlx4_0```.

Using the master nightly install, I ran the following:

```shell
$> mpirun --map-by ppr:1:node --mca btl '^tcp' --mca btl_uct_memory_domains mlx5_0,mlx4_0 ./IMB-RMA
```

This successfully started IMB-RMA, whereas leaving off the btl_uct_memory_domains option has it quit right at the start with the message about not being able to communicate between the two ranks. However, it later seg-faulted, which it doesn't do when I use `--mca osc '^rdma'`. That may be a separate issue... This does suggest that the original error for this issue does look to be simply about rdma complaining when it doesn't have a btl that can do inter-node communication.

Would it be possible to have the rdma osc component not kill the MPI job when it isn't being used? In all test cases I have done, the ucx osc component gets chosen, so there seems to be no need for osc rdma to be killing the MPI job.

Looks like letting the rdma osc component init is somehow behind the segmentation fault. The following invocation leads to a seg fault in IMB-RMA:

```shell
$> mpirun --map-by ppr:1:node --mca btl '^tcp' --mca btl_uct_memory_domains mlx5_0,mlx4_0 ./IMB-RMA
```

The following invocation has IMB-RMA run fine:

```shell
$> mpirun --map-by ppr:1:node --mca btl '^tcp' --mca btl_uct_memory_domains mlx5_0,mlx4_0 --mca osc '^rdma' ./IMB-RMA
```

I thought that perhaps having the uct btl successfully init might lead to the seg fault, but the above implies it isn't. At least, it isn't to blame on its own. The rdma osc seems to be the easy toggle to get the seg fault.
Is this related to #7830? I may have misunderstood what #7830 is dealing with, but it seems quite similar. That is, the rdma osc having issues when btls aren't communicating with all ranks.

I'm trying to use a repository variable in a matrix and then use the matrix variable for a container image, like:
```
---
name: testing

on:

jobs:
  run_test:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        version: ${{ fromJSON(vars.PYTHON_VERSIONS) }}

      - run: echo "${{ vars.PYTHON_VERSIONS }}"

The method is called in DocumentStore.php, l. 173, with a variable `$savedContent` as parameter.
`$savedContent` is initialized in l. 158 of the same file with `fopen(...).
According to [php docs](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.fopen.php), fopen "[r]eturns a file pointer resource on success, or false on failure".

title: system: snapshot default names and other ideas
body: **Important notices** Our forum is located at https://forum.opnsense.org , please consider joining discussions there in stead of using GitHub for these matters. Before you ask a new question, we ask you kindly to acknowledge the following: - [x] I have read the contributing guide lines at https://github.com/opnsense/core/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md - [x] I am convinced that my issue is new after having checked both open and closed issues at https://github.com/opnsense/core/issues?q=is%3Aissue Now that snapshots are in 24.7.3 and received a last minute change as ebf2b587c63 the debate about the "best" default naming are open. The ISO date is probably great, but we don't really need the time unless we want to make it unique but the chances are if someone has two snapshots in the same second the second one doesn't need to be created, which naturally fails. However, when that second has passed the value of the next snapshot is equally debatable. Daily backups are nice and people doing multiple backups per day probably want to annotate their changes more than just timestamps for visibility reasons. The nice thing is that during boot we know what we booted on the console: Something like this should probably be in the dashboard as well. Now back to the topic: The second half of the default snapshot name is probably best used from the currently installed opnsense package so e.g.: `2024-08-29-24.7.1_2` The leading ISO date mostly caters to a sane ability to sort the list. The version gives enough clues about what to expect from the snapshot away from the date (and you can see the creation date for the snapshot anyway). Other thoughts? @sheridans @AdSchellevis @swhite2 @Monviech @pmhausen and everyone else TODO: - [ ] Change default snapshot name - [ ] Remove automatic snapshot naming from bectl.py - [ ] Look at how the boot menu works vs. how it could work - [ ] Sane way for automation in the future - [ ] Consider cron-based snapshots and what their names would be then.... - [ ] Auto-cleanup?! - [ ] Upgrade (major) and update (minor) hooks usefulness and scriptability - [ ] Discuss "N" and "R" nomenclature and why we are now showing a real text instead, maybe as separate columns

comments.body: I like date+version

I was wondering if having an indication of whether the system is applying updates from Regular/Generaly Available  vs Snapshots/Development would be helpful, especially when testing things and moving back and forth between BEs

2024-08-29-R-24.7.1_2 vs 2024-08-S-29-24.7.1_2 or 2024-08-29-D-24.7.1_2

I prefer simplicity and uniqueness to be honest, in which case the timestamp prevents multiple snapshots on the same day overlapping each other. When the version stays the same and someone want to test different types of settings or packages, it's convenient that defaults don't automatically overlap.

Remember, it's just a default, people can change the name any way they like manually...

If anyone else finds themselves here, I forgot to include `secrets: inherit` on the parent .yaml file's job. If this is not included, the child .yaml file will not be able to access the secrets. 

```yaml
jobs:
  build_app: 
    uses: ./.github/workflows/staging_build_app.yaml
    with:
      input_key: value
    secrets: inherit
```

title: [Question] What is the best way to handle multiple feature branches for multiple packages with Conan?
body:
Hi @lasote and @memsharded,

We have a big discussion within the team what is the best solution to handle feature branches for packages which depends on each other. We hope that you can suggest the best way to handle it with Conan.

### Starting point

Let's take your "say"-"hello"-"chat" example from https://github.com/conan-io/examples.git workspace feature. "chat" -requires-> "hello" -requires-> "say".

#### developer task
The implementation has to be refactored for all packages (e.g. in your example the name of the chatting person has to be shown). This will be done in feature branches. 

#### infrastructure
Not sure, but I think it doesn't matter if it is a single mono-repo or three different repos. Let's say there are three git repos.
Additionally there are three CI jobs which depends on each other and which creates each package.
Job_say --> creates "say" --> triggers Job_hello
Job_hello --> creates "hello" --> triggers Job_chat
Job_chat --> creates "chat"

Probably not the best solution to have that dependency defined in CI but that is not necessarily important. The only important thing is, that there are three jobs, one for each package to be more flexible.

### Requirements
Before merging the feature branches into develop branch the features have to be completely tested in combination. Just unit testing "say" is not enough for merge, also "hello" and "chat" have to be build and tested completely.

There has to be a reproducible and safe way to define that special "feature branch" graph for build and testing.
CI and development workflow have to be the same (otherwise one will get something like "locally it works, don't now why CI fails" ;)

### Current approaches
#### Approach 1: Adding branch information to "version" or "channel"
For develop and release builds the "normal" version and channel (testing or stable) will be used.
The CI get's the branch information from current scm, checks branch name and calls `conan create <scm_dir> user/testing_feature_xyz` for "say". This will create "say/0.1@user/testing_feature_xyz". Having the branch information within the "version" is nearly the same approach, so further description is just for channel.

After upload to server there will be a recipe and all packages (build with different settings) with the new reference.

#####  Problems
"hello" has to know the custom channel when building the feature branch. Could be done by "hard-coding" it into the "hello" recipe, but that seems not to be the best solution, especially for merging into develop branch. And "chat" has to know the custom channel of "hello" too.
```python
...
    name = "hello"
    requires = "say/0.1.@user/testing_feature_1"
...
```
and 
```python
...
    name = "chat"
    requires = "hello/0.1.@user/testing_feature_1"
...
```

Patching the scm versioned recipes locally may IMHO not be a solution (e.g. with "find&replace") for CI. But it would be feasible with a lot of scripting.
For development workflow it could work but is very error prone (create "say" with custom channel --> patch "hello" recipe --> create "hello" with custom channel --> patch "chat" recipe --> create "chat" with custom channel).

#### Approach 2: Like approach 1 but with additional Alias package
See description of approach 1. Additionally an alias package would be created which points to the required feature_branch package.

Question 1: How should the alias package be named especially when there are more than just one feature branch plus develop branch which points to `<package>/<version>@<user>/testing`?
Question 2: Which job should create the alias and should it be uploaded too?
Question 3: How to get rid of old packages/cleanup? Having a weekly cron job which checks the current existing branches?

##### Problems
Assuming alias package points to "normal" testing channel which is referenced in recipe `<package>/<version>@<user>/testing` there will be naming clashes / differences betw

Hi!

I'm sorry, I don't have the answer 😞 , I just want to purpose another approach:


**Approach 5: One remote per feature branch**

Without changing the references of the packages or requirements, you can configure Conan in your CI with different remotes depending on the branch you are running. The feature `feature_1` could create a repository in Artifactory and then, CI running branches `feature_1` will add that remote to Conan (first place and maybe remove testing/stable remotes) and consume/upload packages from/to that one. Of course, you will need to propagate the remotes information from one job to another, but I think it would be easier/safer than editing the recipes themselves or introducing an option to handle this.

This approach needs a lot more thinking, it may have many corner cases. Let's see what others suggest.

Hi @jgsogo ,

what a pity that there is no good solution available.
Concerning your approach: We already have two repos. One for testing and one for release (and one additional for third_party stuff). What you describe sounds a bit like an additional staging repo!?! Yes, could work, but there are some issues with that approach:

- The remote has to be always the first in the list (as you already described). Feasible, but then you will have at least two remotes with the same references (staging and testing). First one in staging is used by Conan, but this has to be ensured for every future Conan version. Not sure if you can guarantee this at all?!
- Because of other dependencies in testing-, release- or third_party-repo, the remotes can't be removed.
- The staging repo has to be cleaned after merge. Otherwise one could probably get other "staged" references from this remote which might not be the expected ones. Let's assume that there is also a requirement from "chat" to "goodbye" which is not part of refactoring and which has to come from testing repo.

Probably there are some more issues with that approach.

But thanks a lot for your reply.

No solution yet, or not a solution that comes out of my mind right now, but this is something we want to address, so all the feedback related to this is so important.

> * The remote has to be always the first in the list (as you already described). Feasible, but then you will have at least two remotes with the same references (staging and testing). First one in staging is used by Conan, but this has to be ensured for every future Conan version. Not sure if you can guarantee this at all?!

Yes, the iteration order of the remotes is stable, so this shouldn't be an issue. A new reference will be retrieved from the first remote that contains that reference. If your _staging_ repo is the first in the list, it will be the one used.

> * The staging repo has to be cleaned after merge. Otherwise one could probably get other "staged" references from this remote which might not be the expected ones. Let's assume that there is also a requirement from "chat" to "goodbye" which is not part of refactoring and which has to come from testing repo.

I'm suggesting one _staging_ repo per feature, and this staging repo will only be added to Conan in those CI jobs related to the feature. After merging the feature, this staging repo won't be used anymore, so it can be removed or not.

Even more, there should be a new staging repo for each feature (for each branch) within each library. So, for a new branch `featA`, one developer will make a PR to `say` repo, it will trigger CI as yo

Ok got your approach. 
Because of high infrastructure interaction (create and delete remote) this should be a conan and artifactory/ bintray feature. 

Something like `conan remote add testing https://url` and `conan upload <reference> -r testing -push-stage=say_feature_1` and `conan move <reference> -r testing -pop-stage` done in the last job. 

Just as an idea for further discussions.

Have a look at nexus concept for maven. https://help.sonatype.com/repomanager2/staging-releases/managing-staging-repositories 

It should be quite similar.

Conan new CI tutorial in https://docs.conan.io/2/ci_tutorial/tutorial.html now summarizes best practices and new tools, like using lockfiles, multiple repositories (but not one per branch) and promotions. The ``conan-extensions`` repo even contain implementation for ``conan art:promote`` command.

Closing this ticket, for further feedback better create new tickets based on the new CI tutorial contents too. Thanks for the feedback.
